ques.p: To ask the Secretary of State for the Home Department, how many proposed Freedom of Information responses were awaiting clearance from (a) the Communications Directorate and (b) special advisers on 31 August 2026, and how many in each category had been awaiting that clearance for (i) up to 20, (ii) 21 to 40 and (iii) more than 40 working days.

reply.p: The Home Office is the largest recipient of Freedom of Information requests across central government and received over 8,700 requests in 2025. The cases shown in the table represent a point-in-time snapshot of requests within the Communications Directorate and Special Adviser review processes and account for a relatively small proportion of the overall volume of FOI requests handled by the Department.
Cases within the Communications Directorate and Special Adviser review processes (information extracted and validated on 28 September 2026)

td.p: Within wider Special Adviser Referral Process

reply.p: Note: The Department does not routinely retain historical reports showing the stage reached within the Special Adviser review process at a specific point in time. The figures therefore reflect information extracted and validated on 28 September 2026. Cases awaiting consideration by Special Advisers have been presented separately from cases elsewhere within the wider Special Adviser referral process.

The figures are management information derived from the Home Office's case management system and supplementary information provided by the Special Adviser Private Office. They have not undergone formal quality assurance.

publicwhip.major-heading: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs
publicwhip.minor-heading: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs: Remote Working

ques.p: To ask the Secretary of State for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs, how many and what proportion of civil servants in her Department were on permanent home working contracts in 2025.

reply.p: As of December 2025, there were 814 civil servants on home working contracts, equating to 13% of the total number of civil servants in Defra.

publicwhip.minor-heading: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs: Facilities Agreements

ques.p: To ask the Secretary of State for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs, what was the total cost of facility time to the department in (a) 2023-24, (b) 2024-25 and (c) 2025-26; and what was the headcount number of facility time staff in each; how many were 100% facility time; and whether funding was provided for trade union activities in each of those years.

reply.p: The information on trade union facility time for 2023/24 and 2024/25 is publicly available through the Defra Annual Report and Accounts, on GOV.UK.

For the Defra bargaining unit in 2025/26, the total cost of trade union facility time was £119,469 and the headcount of staff claiming facility time was 23 people. Nobody was allocated 100% trade union facility time and no funding was provided for trade union activities.

ques.p: To ask the Secretary of State for Defence, pursuant to the answer of 27 July 2026, to question 17492 on Guided Weapons, by when does he plan to have a) defined, b) sequenced and c) implemented arrangements to support a future UK-France Complex Weapons cooperation.

reply.p: Bilateral discussions to define and implement the most efficient, iterative options to support a UK-France Complex Weapons Joint Portfolio Office are underway, expanding on a recent senior bilateral engagement and current Lancaster House cooperation and resourcing.
